purpose: Broad Run is the one basin where four independent sources converge. It should be a named case in the paper, not a row in a basin table.

concentration.source: Watersheds.geojson (county layer) x basin_stress.json building attribution
concentration.statement: 72.5% of the county's data centers sit on 19.9% of its land -- a 3.6x concentration. Bull Run, the LARGER watershed, is at parity. Every other basin is essentially empty.

the_gage_problem.issue: The flow denominator for the basin carrying 72.5% of the fleet comes from a gage decommissioned in 1986. It never observed any part of the 23-month severe drought now underway, and stopped forty years before the demand it is being used to assess.
the_gage_problem.consequence: Both sides of the basin-stress ratio are anchored to different and mutually inconsistent periods: demand is indexed to a cooling-degree-day series that has risen 27-33% over the record, while supply is divided by a gage record that ended in 1986.

warming.context: Of 17 stations in the Prince William / Occoquan group, 15 have positive slopes, 1 is exactly 0.000 (Catoctin Creek 1ACAX004.57) and 1 is negative (Pohick Creek 1APOH005.36). A sign test on the 16 non-ties gives 15 of 16, two-tailed p = 0.0005. Broad Run 1ABRB002.15 is the ONLY station individually significant at p<0.05.
warming.statewide: Across all 413 Virginia stations only 49 (12%) are individually significant -- but 47 of those 49 are warming and 2 cooling. State the 12% honestly; the 47:2 split carries the inference.

sign_test.CORRECTION: An earlier draft claimed '16 of 17 positive, p ~ 0.0001'. Recounted from the source layer: 15 positive, not 16, and the correct two-tailed sign-test p is 0.0005, not 0.0001.

binding_condition.note: Computed on the CORRECTED observed monthly shape. Under the superseded CDD model this read 28.3% in July; the binding month moved to September and the magnitude roughly halved when the shape was fixed.

convergence: Broad Run carries 72.5% of the fleet on 19.9% of the land; its flow denominator comes from a gage dead since 1986; it is the only county stream with a statistically significant warming trend; and it is in the worst drought of the 132-year instrumental record. Four independent sources, one basin, all pointing the same way.
